candidates.rationale: Margin expansion at a firm already converting assets to sales efficiently is durable operating leverage rather than a one-off cost cut, and sell-side margin assumptions are revised with a one-to-two quarter lag.
ROE manufactured by the balance sheet rather than operations carries refinancing and distress risk, and firms actively adding debt this quarter face interest expense not yet in consensus earnings.
An earnings yield only pays if the earnings are cash; the accrual rank strips out firms whose EPS is inflated by working-capital accruals that reverse in later quarters.

A cash-backed firm whose daily range is wide relative to peers is absorbing liquidity-driven flow rather than news, so its swings revert, while the same width in an accrual-heavy firm is genuine bad news being priced.

A one-week drawdown is fundable noise at a high-margin, low-leverage firm and early distress pricing at a thin-margin levered one, so the same dip should be bought in the first and sold in the second.
An improving return on assets is repriced only when investors show up; the week-over-month dollar volume ratio measures the attention that converts a quarterly fundamental improvement into price.
Book value per share compounding faster than the price is retained earnings the market has not capitalized, and the gap closes as successive balance sheets make the accumulation visible.
Two-week price pressure means accumulation in a cheap-on-book name and chasing in an expensive one, so the valuation level decides which side of the same short-run flow to take.
Operating profitability above reported ROA means interest, tax, or one-off charges are depressing the bottom line; those items mean-revert while the operating strength persists.
Earnings improved over the last quarter while the price failed to make a new high, so the improvement is uncapitalized and the next confirming report closes the gap.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: EXPLORE. Propose 10 NEW factor expressions.

Direction for this island

Archive coverage so far. Each niche is (IC half-life bucket / data family /
turnover bucket). Aim at the emptiest ones: a factor that fills an empty niche
is worth more to this search than a slightly better version of a full one.
  niche                                   count  best fitness  capacity

  medium/price_volume/high                   0             -         8
  medium/fundamental/low                     0             -         8

  medium/mixed/low                           2         4.355         8

  slow/price_volume/high                     2         0.824         8
  slow/fundamental/low                       1         3.731         8

Sub-expressions already heavily used by the published Alpha101 set. Reusing one
of these wholesale will be rejected as a paraphrase; they are listed so you can
avoid them, not so you can vary them cosmetically.
  (($high + $low) / 2)   (in 5 published alphas)
  ($high + $low)   (in 5 published alphas)
  DELAY($close, 1)   (in 5 published alphas)
  TS_DELTA($close, 1)   (in 5 published alphas)
  TS_MEAN($volume, 20)   (in 5 published alphas)
  ($volume / (1e-08 + TS_MEAN($volume, 20)))   (in 4 published alphas)
  (1e-08 + TS_MEAN($volume, 20))   (in 4 published alphas)
  ($close - DELAY($close, 1))   (in 4 published alphas)
  TS_DELTA($close, 7)   (in 4 published alphas)
  (((DELAY($close, 20) - DELAY($close, 10)) / 10) - ((DELAY($close, 10) - $close) / 10))   (in 3 published alphas)
  ((DELAY($close, 20) - DELAY($close, 10)) / 10)   (in 3 published alphas)
  (($close - DELAY($close, 1)) * -(1))   (in 3 published alphas)

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Budget one long time-series term per candidate. A single 126d fundamental delta was accepted (1.589), but two 126d fundamental deltas combined, or any 252d window on $roa/$roe/$return, landed at 0.869-0.882 coverage.
  2. Stop submitting CS_ZSCORE times CS_ZSCORE products. Both died on the cheap screen (leverage x TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) at 0.57, 5d return reversal x $roe at 0.59). The accepted mixed factors use a cross-sectional fundamental rank as the base and a raw price ratio as the multiplier.
  3. Pure price-geometry expressions with no fundamental field were the worst cheap-screen scores of the round (0.36 and 0.41). Do not send TS_MAX/TS_MIN/high-low range constructions unless a fundamental score leads the expression.
  4. $accrual_gap times a normalized intraday range is this island's best vein (3.570 and 2.250 accepted). Extend it by varying the window structure of the range and its normalizer (2/5/21 day mixes), not by swapping the denominator's scale, which returned rho 0.839 against an archived sibling.
  5. Re-dressing an archived factor never clears correlation: raw $roa against RANK($roa) is 1.000, and attaching a strictly positive bounded range multiplier to RANK($roa) still leaves rho 0.860. To decorrelate from a single-field archived rank, subtract a second cross-sectional rank or change sign structure instead of multiplying.
  6. Price-scaling a fundamental and adding a plain quality rank works ($book_per_share/$open with $roe scored 3.155), but pairing a price-scaled fundamental with a 252d volatility term failed coverage at 0.869. Keep the second leg a contemporaneous cross-sectional rank.
  7. Crossover needs a real subtree splice. Two proposals scored only 2 shared nodes because they wrapped a whole parent in a fresh multiplier; each parent should contribute a named field plus its own transform.
  8. Keep a within-round proposal ledger for the $roa and $accrual_gap templates. A roa-delta minus return-mean pair was proposed twice and burned a slot as a duplicate.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
Leave `parent_ids` empty and `changed_node` empty for EXPLORE.
